content.text:
I built `spec.vl.json` as a heatmap: one row per depth from 2 m at the top to 40 m at the bottom, one column per month, and colour showing the monthly mean temperature in °C. It renders with status OK and no errors or warnings. Months where a depth has no data show as grey cells. The figure shows gaps at 2 m in 2019 and 2024, at 5 m in 2023 and late 2025, and at 40 m around late 2022 to 2023.

The caption says that every year shallow water warms strongly and peaks in August–September, while deep water stays cool and peaks later, in autumn, with a much smaller swing. I checked this against the data outside the deliverable. Averaged by calendar month, 2 m peaks at about 17.7 °C in September and 40 m peaks at about 9.0 °C in October.

```
REPORT
deliverable: spec.vl.json
requirements:
  R1: done - daily means averaged per UTC year-month and depth inside the spec (aggregate transform)
  R2: done - x axis has all 95 months Feb 2018–Dec 2025, labelled at each January
  R3: done - no rect is drawn for a missing depth-month; grey background shows as an empty cell; no imputation
  R4: done - y axis labelled "2 m"…"40 m", sorted by number from shallow to deep
  R5: done - colour legend titled "Mean temperature (°C)"
  R6: done - title plus a one-sentence caption on the main pattern (subtitle), plus a note on data source and grey cells
assumptions:
  - Monthly mean = unweighted mean of daily means (not weighted by n_obs)
  - Months are UTC calendar months; ISO dates parsed as UTC
  - Rows with empty or non-numeric temperature are dropped before aggregating
limitations:
  - The x axis is ordinal: it lists only months with data at some depth. All 95 months have data, but a month with no data at any depth would be dropped rather than shown as an empty column
  - A month with only a few days of data is shown like a full month; the tooltip gives the day count
  - The turbo colour scheme is not perceptually uniform; use the tooltip for exact values
  - The caption was written after checking the data and is fixed text, not computed in the spec
```
